title: Low Blood Glucose (Hypoglycemia)
org: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16 (last reviewed July 2021): low is usually below 70 mg/dL; two types of diabetes pills can cause lows (sulfonylureas, meglitinides); skipped or delayed meals, alcohol, illness and more physical activity than usual lower glucose, activity for up to 24 hours afterwards; treat with 15 to 20 g, wait 15 minutes, recheck; with medicines that slow carbohydrate digestion use glucose tablets or gel; glucagon by injection or nasal spray for severe lows.

title: Diabetes Symptoms
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16 through the web fetcher (cdc.gov refuses curl): frequent urination, thirst and hunger, weight loss, fatigue, irritability, blurry vision, frequent urinary tract or yeast infections; numbness or tingling in hands or feet listed among symptoms more common in type 2.

title: Asthma Action Plan (2020, sample plan)
org: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16 (PDF): green zone (no cough, wheeze, chest tightness or shortness of breath, day or night; usual activities); yellow zone (cough, wheeze, chest tightness or shortness of breath, or waking at night, or some but not all usual activities); red zone (very short of breath, quick-relief medicines have not helped, cannot do usual activities, or same or worse after 24 hours in yellow); danger signs (trouble walking and talking due to shortness of breath; lips or fingernails blue): go to the hospital or call an ambulance now.

title: Asthma Attack
org: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16: call 9-1-1 if medicines are not relieving symptoms during an attack or breathing is still very hard; for young children call 9-1-1 if drowsy, confused, blue tint to skin and lips, or fast heartbeat.

title: Pictograph: Oxygen Tank Safety
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16: keep oxygen tanks at least 5 feet from a heat source, open flames or electrical devices; never use a candle, match, lighter or other open flame near medical oxygen. Replaces the unreadable NFPA tip sheet (nfpa.org returned 500/404) for the 5-ft rule.

title: Oxygen Therapy: Using Oxygen Safely
licence_note: Copyright American Lung Association. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16: oxygen is non-flammable but supports combustion; never change the prescribed flow rate; no smoking, No Smoking and No Open Flames signs; heat and flame at least five feet away; no oxygen while cooking with gas; no aerosols, vapor rubs, petroleum jelly or oil-based lotions; never oil the unit; liquid oxygen upright; not in a closet or trunk; turn off when not in use; concentrators several inches from walls and curtains.

title: Gestational age
org: MedlinePlus, US National Library of Medicine (A.D.A.M.)
licence_note: A.D.A.M. encyclopedia content on MedlinePlus (copyrighted). Read by R10 on 2026-11-16: gestational age is measured in weeks from the first day of the last menstrual cycle; a normal pregnancy ranges from 38 to 42 weeks; born before 37 weeks is premature.

title: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025 (9th edition, full text)
org: US Department of Agriculture and US Department of Health and Human Services
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16 (PDF), chapter 6 table of estimated calorie needs compared to prepregnancy needs: lactation first 6 months +330 calories, second 6 months +400 calories (pregnancy 2nd trimester +340, 3rd +452). The older index key usda-hhs-dietary-guidelines-for-americans-2020-2025-4b2013 now points at the dietaryguidelines.gov landing page, which announces the newer edition.

title: How to Clean, Sanitize, and Store Infant Feeding Items
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16 through the web fetcher: clean basin used only for infant feeding items, hot soapy water, air dry thoroughly; sanitize daily (or more often) if the baby is less than 2 months old, born prematurely, or has a weakened immune system; boil method 5 minutes, remove with clean tongs; do not rinse after sanitizing. The index key cdc-cleaning-infant-feeding-items points at a URL that now returns 404.

title: Cow's Milk and Milk Alternatives
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R10 on 2026-11-16 through the web fetcher: whole cow's milk can be introduced at 12 months (but not before); 12 through 23 months, about 2 servings of dairy a day, unflavored, unsweetened whole milk is one option; fortified dairy alternatives are the only milk alternatives that help meet dairy needs, not before 12 months, discuss with the child's doctor.
